events.title: 10-year Treasury yield jumps back above 5% as oil gains, more Fed hikes expected
events.summary: U.S. Treasury yields jumped on Thursday, with the 10-year again topping 5%, alongside a move higher in oil prices and expectations of further Federal Reserve hikes ahead. The yield on the 10-year U.S. Treasury note — the benchmark for mortgages, auto loans and credit card debt — was up 4 basis points at 5.032%. It earlier hit 5.0583%, its highest level since Oct. 22. The 2-year Treasury note yield, which is more sensitive to short-term Fed interest rate decisions, was 7 basis points higher at 4.797%. The longer-dated 30-year Treasury note yield — which often moves on geopolitical developments — rose 2 basis points to 5.37%. One basis point equals 0.01%, or 1/100th of 1%, and yields and prices move inversely to one another. The rise in oil prices came after President Donald Trump said, " we don't need a deal with Iran ," raising concerns that an end to the war was not in sight. West Texas Intermediate futures gained 0.38% to $86.86 a barrel, while Brent crude rose 0.99% to $93.60 per barrel. Meanwhile, Tuesday's hotter-than-expected consumer price index reading has investors anticipating more rate increases from the Fed. Goldman Sachs added another rate hike to its forecast on Wednesday, now expecting an adidtional a 25-basis-point increase in March. Traders are pricing in 100% odds of an increase in December, with roughly 13% calling for a 50 basis point hike, according to the CME Group's FedWatch tool. More domestic data will be released this week, which will provide fresh insights into the U.S. economic picture. On Friday, the latest monthly producer price inflation print, which tracks wholesale inflation, is expected to show a 0.4% rise in October, down from the 1.3% surge in September. Before that, investors are also looking out for October's home sales report from the National Association of Realtors, due later Thursday. Existing home sales rose by 1.5% in September to 3.99 million, up from a two-year low the previous month, and are expected to reach 4 million last month, according to Trading Economics estimates.

events.title: Jensen Huang, an architect of the AI boom, resigns as Nvidia CEO
events.summary: Jensen Huang resigned as CEO of Nvidia after he reportedly had two affairs, including one with a purported Chinese spy. Why it matters: It's impossible to overstate how critical Huang is to Nvidia, to the AI buildout, to the stock market and economy. His departure could, per Wall Street sources, be the catalyst that endangers a ballooning AI bubble. Driving the news: Nvidia's board named longtime CFO Colette Kress interim CEO, while launching a search for a permanent replacement. Kress, who joined Nvidia in 2013, will continue serving as CFO while overseeing the company. Harvey C. Jones was appointed Nvidia's first-ever board chair. The board said it expects Nvidia's operations, customer commitments and product roadmap to continue without interruption. Zoom out: Huang's resignation follows revelations about two extramarital relationships. The New York Times reported Wednesday that Huang had a relationship with Kimberly Powell, a senior Nvidia executive who reports to him. Nvidia's board had previously launched an independent investigation into Huang's relationship with Alice Huang, a Chinese businesswoman identified by U.S. intelligence as a Chinese intelligence asset. Nvidia did not provide a reason for Huang's resignation in Thursday's announcement, which comes after reports that the board had an emergency meeting over whether to oust the CEO. By the numbers: Nvidia shares fell more than 10% after news of Huang's resignation. This is breaking news.

events.title: Who could replace Jensen Huang as Nvidia's chief executive?
events.summary: Arm's boss Rene Haas (L), Nvidia's Colette Kress (C) and Chris Malachowsky (R) have been named as possible successors Published 12 November 2026, 10:37 GMT Nvidia is facing a scenario few would have considered until very recently - a future without Jensen Huang. The chief executive and co-founder of the AI chip-making giant is at the centre of a major scandal over reports of extramarital affairs, one of which was with a woman suspected of being a Chinese spy. Nvidia's board is reportedly meeting to discuss whether to replace Huang. But finding the right person to lead the business that Huang helped create more than three decades ago and turned into the world's second most valuable company - after Apple - is a challenge. We take a look at which candidates have emerged as potential successors. Colette Kress is chief financial officer at Nvidia Colette Kress, Nvidia's chief financial officer, has been tipped as someone who could steady the ship in the interim, and possibly stop its share price from plunging even further. An industry veteran for more than 30 years, Kress previously held high positions at tech firms like Cisco and Microsoft. Kress, who also serves as Nvidia's executive vice president, has seen the firm's transformation from making chips for video games in the early 1990s to becoming an AI semiconductor powerhouse. She "fronts every earnings call" alongside Huang and is a "familiar and trusted voice for the market at a time when it badly needs one," said Josh Gilbert, an analyst at investment firm eToro. But doing the job permanently could be a different story, said Gilbert, as the firm, known for its edge in technology, could want an engineer in the chair. Chris Malachowsky is one of Nvidia's three co-founders Another option is Chris Malachowsky, who founded Nvidia alongside Huang and Curtis Priem, and is the only executive that shares the same level of seniority. Malachowsky has played a key part in developing the company's computing technology. Ian Buck, who oversees Nvidia's high-performance computing business, has also emerged as a potential candidate if the company is keen to put an engineer in the top job. Buck was among the early pioneers who helped popularise the use of graphic processors beyond gaming applications. "He could protect Nvidia's technological edge, but his ability to manage the wider commercial relationships and geopolitical challenges would face scrutiny," said Charu Chanana, investment strategist at investment bank Saxo. Today, Nvidia's leading processors are widely regarded as the gold standard for AI development. Huang's children also work at Nvidia in executive positions but are relatively young and inexperienced. Nvidia is likely to favour an internal appointment initially but could look externally for a more permanent replacement, said Jun Bei Liu, founder and lead portfolio manager at Ten Cap. Several names of tech entrepreneurs outside of Nvidia have been floated by experts. Liu said Apple's former chief executive, Tim Cook, could be a possible choice as someone familiar with managing global supply chains, though she questioned whether he would be willing to leave the iPhone maker, where he is the chair. Apple's Tim Cook (R) with Jensen Huang (L) and his wife Lori Huang at the White House Liu and Chanana also suggested Rene Haas, chief executive of Arm Holdings, the UK chipmaking giant. Nvidia's processors are made with the help of chipmakers around the world, including Taiwan's TSMC and South Korea's SK Hynix and Samsung. Rene Haas is the boss of Arm Holdings Haas is familiar with leading a publicly-listed company and would bring semiconductor experience, though Nvidia's business model is considerably different from Arm's, said Chanana. "The challenge is finding someone who can combine Jensen's technical understanding, strategic vision and relationships across the global technology industry," Liu said. Ten Cap's Liu believes it is a matter of time in terms of Huang stepping down as Nvidia's chief executive. "The issue is no longer simply about personal conduct," she said. "It is about corporate governance, national security concerns and maintaining confidence in the leadership of one of the world's most strategically important companies." Several major investment firms have downgraded their forecasts for the chip giant - a rare shift given investors' longstanding optimism about the company. Nvidia's chief executive Jensen Huang Stacy Rasgon, senior analyst in US semiconductors at Bernstein Research, wrote in a note to investors that "our gut tells us we probably haven't fully probed the depths of what might be found here". Rasgon halved Bernstein's share price target for Nvidia and said: "We've had enough and prefer to watch from the sidelines.

events.title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigns amid spy, affair scandals
events.summary: Jensen Huang at GTC Berlin last month. | Photo: Soeren Stache / picture alliance via Getty Images Nvidia's board has separated from Jensen Huang, its longtime co-founder, president, and CEO, after reports of two extramarital affairs - one with an alleged Chinese spy and one with an Nvidia executive who reported to Huang. events.title: ‘It is much, much faster’: could China’s battery-swapping e-trucks be the answer to EV range anxiety?
events.summary: Battery maker CATL aims to have 2,000 swapping stations in China by the end of 2027 and to bring the tech to Europe E very day, Wang Bing drives his big electric lorry to send around five tonnes of goods between the cities of Haikou and Dongfang on Hainan, a tropical island in southern China . A round trip covers about 500 kilometres (310 miles). But refuelling is not something Wang worries about. “When my battery runs low, I just drive my truck into a battery-swapping station to get a fully charged one,” says the 53-year-old, who shares the journey with a colleague in eight-hour shifts. Wang has been a lorry driver for nearly three decades. In the first two of those, he drove conventional lorries fuelled by diesel. About five years ago, he began driving an electric model after the logistics company he worked for upgraded its fleet. In July this year, his old e-truck, which used conventional plug-in charging, was replaced by one with a swappable battery. In the past, Wang had to spend an hour and half charging his battery each time, but with his new truck, it takes just five minutes or so to have a drained battery removed and a fresh one replaced. “I am very happy,” he says. Battery swapping is not new in China, where more than 400,000 e-trucks (or over 90% of the global total ) were sold last year. The Chinese carmaker Nio commercialised the technology nearly a decade ago for smaller electric vehicles (EVs). But in 2023, the Chinese battery behemoth CATL launched a battery-swapping system for electric lorries through a subsidiary brand called Qiji Energy. To Wang, the biggest advantage of the technology is the time it saves. “It is much, much faster,” he says. “I don’t even need to leave my truck when the battery is being swapped.” This swiftness builds on the cost advantage e-trucks already have over their fossil-fuelled peers when it comes to refuelling. “Electricity is cheaper than oil,” Wang says. The per-kilometre fuelling cost for an e-truck works out about 1.1 yuan (12p) in Hainan, he says, significantly lower than that for a diesel truck, which exceeds 2 yuan (22p) a kilometre. “That means my e-truck can save more than 20,000 yuan (£2,200) per month,” Wang says. When a truck approaches a battery-swapping station, the station’s cameras automatically identify the type of battery it uses by checking its number plate. “All the driver needs to do is to drive the truck into a designated area, and the battery will be swapped completely automatically,” says Wei Jiuchun, 46, a test driver at a Qiji Energy battery-swapping station in Suzhou, east China. Wei’s job is to help the station test its system for different models of heavy trucks and under different weather conditions. It is not just time and fuel costs the technology saves but, in China, the initial lump sum a buyer has to put down to get an e-truck, says Mao Shiyue, a Beijing-based researcher at the International Council on Clean Transportation (ICCT). The upfront purchase price for an e-truck is significantly higher than for a comparable diesel model, a major obstacle for those vehicles’ wider adoption in many parts of the world. In China, a customer opting for battery swapping typically buys an e-truck without a battery, and then rents the battery from a service provider. As the cost of a battery is about 40% of an e-truck’s price, the business model can make e-trucks a lot more affordable, Mao says. The technology can also help minimise the pressure EV charging brings to the power grid, according to Mao, because swapping stations have more flexibility to spread out the charging time for the depleted batteries. “If the grid sees a spike in electricity demand during peak hours, those stations can even act as an energy-storage station by returning the electricity stored in their batteries back to the grid to ease the strain,” he says. The planet's most important stories. Get all the week's environment news - the good, the bad and the essential CATL, the world’s biggest battery manufacturer, is a key player in promoting battery swapping for heavy trucks in China. The company’s support for the technology is critical for its large-scale rollout, says Phate Zhang, the founder of CnEVPost, a Shanghai-based outlet focusing on EVs. CATL plans to put 900 battery-swapping stations into operation across China by the end of this year, expanding its current network twice more. By the end of 2027, it wants the number to reach 2,000. The company has also teamed up with the London-based renewable energy supplier Octopus to bring the technology to Europe. It intends to open its first group of battery-swapping “mega hubs” in the UK next year, and a network of more than 30 hubs in Europe by 2035. In China, battery-swapping is still a minority charging method for its rapidly growing e-truck fleet.

events.title: A new AI model wants to read between the lines
events.summary: The Scoop New York-based AI startup millionways on Thursday launched its new AI model that claims to offer insight into human intent and motivations. The company also told Semafor it has raised $6 million in US funding, with investors including football stars Jason Kelce and DK Metcalf. The Thorsten-4 model was born out of a research project in Germany in which dozens of psychologists interviewed more than 7,000 people about their personal lives and aspirations. That data — which the psychologists labeled by hand to capture what people’s words revealed about their motives and thinking — was used to train the model. Millionways cofounders Martin Cordsmeier and Max Weidemann argue that understanding is missing from regular AI models, which are trained on internet text. They see the model as particularly useful in sales and executive hiring, where a search firm could prompt it to evaluate an interview transcript to gauge how a candidate will behave under pressure. “We can add a level of human understanding that the language models cannot get to by themselves,” Weidemann said, adding that the model should be “a decision-making support tool rather than the ultimate decision-maker.” J.D.’s view Enterprises are increasingly injecting task- and industry-specific models into their tech stacks, rather than defaulting to the frontier models for every task. Just this week, leading voice AI company ElevenLabs, for example, announced a healthcare-focused version of its new transcription model. This gives CIOs more choice and customization, but it also adds the burden of testing whether specialized models actually beat fast-improving frontier ones. Cordsmeier and Weidemann ran our conversation for this story through Thorsten-4, which deduced that I was most focused on relationship-building and being conscientious: “You move between logic and intuition, and tough questions energized you.” (I’ll take the compliment!) I ran a transcript of the same call through Anthropic’s new Claude Fable 5.2 model and asked for a psychology analysis: Claude also gave a solid assessment, though it was less sure of itself, focusing more on the job I was doing than on me as a person. It (correctly) noted that my “unstated goal was source cultivation.”

events.title: Instacart wants to deliver supplies to your favorite bar or restaurant
events.summary: Instacart is working with Provi on same-day delivery for nonalcoholic items like garnishes and mixers to restaurants and bars. Yuki Iwamura/Bloomberg via Getty Images Instacart struck a partnership with alcohol marketplace Provi, the companies said on Thursday. Provi will offer Instacart delivery of non-alcoholic items, such as garnishes, to bars and restaurants. The agreement moves Instacart deeper into business-to-business sales. Instacart is getting into delivering last-minute cocktail ingredients and supplies to bars and restaurants. The delivery app has struck a partnership with business-to-business alcohol marketplace Provi, the companies confirmed to Business Insider on Thursday. Instacart will offer same-day delivery of items, including mixers and paper products from grocery stores when ordered through Provi's website and app. The partnership won't include alcohol delivery, the companies said. In the US, laws require alcohol brands to send their products to restaurants and retailers through distributors as part of a three-tiered system. Instead, Instacart and Provi will work together on " rapid delivery as fast as possible" on items that restaurants and bars need in a pinch, such as extra limes for margaritas and napkins for special events, Provi CEO Matthew Tucker said. Many also receive weekly deliveries from more established restaurant distributors. "What we are trying to solve for is that last-minute out-of-stock," Tucker told Business Insider. The partnership expands Instacart's business-to-business offerings. The delivery service got its start by bringing groceries to individual shoppers' doorsteps but has offered business delivery through a separate division since 2023. Its customers include the Four Seasons resort chain and Van Leeuwen Ice Cream. Working with Provi allows Instacart to reach bars and restaurants "where they are shopping today," said Andrew Nodes, vice president and general manager of Instacart Business and Supply Chain. "Now, when a bar or restaurant runs out of herbs or straws mid-service, they have a same-day solution that helps them operate smoothly without missing a beat," Nodes said. It's the first time that Provi is selling non-alcoholic items, Tucker said. The partnership is also coming online at a busy time: the weeks leading up to Thanksgiving and Christmas are when Provi's website and app see the most customer engagement of the year, according to the company. Provi users will see an option to order those items on the platform and will be redirected to Instacart to complete the purchase, he said. While small, many of the products that Provi and Instacart plan to sell are key to driving sales and avoiding customer disappointment, Tucker added. Drinks tend to be the most profitable items at many bars and restaurants. "If you don't have the garnishes," he said, "you aren't able to sell some of your highest-margin products." Restaurants are also dealing with labor shortages resulting from immigration raids , he said. That means many establishments have fewer staff than ever to make quick grocery runs to keep bars stocked. "When you have a problem with your labor, you have a problem operating your restaurant," Tucker said. Do you have a story idea about Instacart? events.title: Warby Parker's rival to Meta glasses is here. I got an early look.
events.summary: I tried out the new smart glasses at Warby Parker's book-themed pop-up. Henry Chandonnet/Business Insider I tried Warby Parker's new smart glasses, built with Google and Samsung. While testing the glasses, I wondered: What made these different from Meta glasses? My answer: not much. There's a new set of smart glasses in town. Warby Parker opened presales on Thursday for its Intelligent Eyewear collection, a partnership with Google and Samsung. It's Google's first return to consumer eyewear since the whole "Glasshole" debacle . These glasses film, translate, and answer questions with AI. Those use cases might sound familiar: Meta glasses do the same things. "This is the kind of product that, on the surface, may seem similar to other devices," Warby Parker co-CEO Dave Gilboa told me. "But, as soon as you put it on, start demoing the functionality, and do that head-to-head, a lot of the differences become pretty clear." So, I spent a rainy Friday morning traipsing around Warby Parker's New York pop-up to figure out what makes these glasses different. My answer: not much. What the glasses do Warby Parker's glasses have Gemini built into them. That means users can ask the standard chatbot questions: What's my schedule? What should I text back? What's my horoscope? The glasses also have visual intelligence, an added perk. They can describe the room you're looking at, or give directions based on the street in front of you. All of these conversations are verbal, meaning glasses users must speak aloud to their devices. That's a bit awkward: Am I really going to say out loud, "Gemini, where am I going?" on the streets of New York? Meta glasses have the same problem; they assume we're comfortable saying everything at all times. Warby Parker's New York pop-up is themed "Literature Land" and includes several ways to test the smart glasses. Henry Chandonnet/Business Insider I found it difficult to weave between conversations. After Gemini told me something, I'd repeat it back to someone else in the room. But Gemini took my repetition as a response and kept asking me questions. It became sonically overwhelming. Users can also prompt the glasses from their phones, but then why have the glasses in the first place? Some of the tech also seemed too early to use, like the translation feature . Talking to a Spanish faux-retail worker at the pop-up, I asked my glasses to translate what he said into English. It switched the language slowly, inching through each word. My biggest takeaway from the demo: this tech is cool! It's cool just like Meta glasses are cool. It's nice that I can ask what book I'm thinking of or take a picture without taking out my phone, a black hole I'm bound to get sucked into. The frames come in three styles and start at $395. Warby Parker took its time developing them, focusing on style above all. "This is a fashion product," said co-CEO Neil Blumenthal . "At its core, it's someone's identity." I liked the style of Warby Parker's smart glasses. They weren't bulky or uncomfortable. Henry Chandonnet/Business Insider There were trade-offs, and the company spent "hundreds of hours" figuring out how to maximize battery life without making the glasses too big, Gilboa said. Nobody wants to be Evan Spiegel with his ears folded down from heavy glasses. They did look good. So do Meta glasses (the normal ones, not the chunky ones with the screen and neural band). 'Pervert' panic risks Meta glasses have run into another problem: their " pervert glasses " reputation. Even with a light to indicate when the wearer is filming, Meta glasses were thrown into controversy after men used them to unknowingly film women. The company has introduced updates to brick the filming abilities of users physically tampering with the light and banned some harassers' Instagram accounts . The Warby Parker glasses have a similar light that indicates camera use and anti-tampering features. The company says it also redacts faces before images are analyzed by Gemini and that camera visuals aren't used for AI training or ad targeting. Warby Parker's smart glasses come in three styles. Henry Chandonnet/Business Insider Still, launching camera glasses in the current environment carries risk. Warby Parker, Google, and Samsung could easily be ensnared in the same blowback that Meta is facing. "For someone to wear it all day, every day, it has to provide real utility to them," Gilboa said. "It also has to be a product that people around them are comfortable with. We think we've achieved both of those elements." I pushed back. The " pervert glasses " pushback sprung up right in the middle of these glasses' development. What were the CEOs' reactions? "Our reaction is we should all be concerned about privacy," Blumenthal responded. Read the original article on Business Insider

events.title: Disney's 'Star Wars' is coming to Cosm domes ahead of 50th anniversary as part of multiyear film deal
events.summary: Cosm has partnered with Disney on a multiyear, multifilm deal that will kick off with "Star Wars: A New Hope" early next year. This is Cosm's third studio deal — it already has partnerships with Universal and Warner Bros. — and sixth theatrical release. Cosm is working directly with studios Lucasfilm and Industrial Light and Magic as well as creative studio MakeMake to create the visuals and the sound mixing for a unique presentation of the film. On Thursday, the immersive entertainment technology company announced a new studio partnership with The Walt Disney Company that will bring the original "Star Wars" to its domes early next year as part of a multiyear, multifilm collaboration. The financial terms of the deal were not disclosed. Cosm's massive concave screens will drop film fans into a galaxy far, far away starting in March, just ahead of the Academy Award-winning film's 50th anniversary in May. "We are thrilled to add the Disney partnership," Alexis Scalice, head of Cosm Studios, told CNBC. "We do look for those opportunities of these like anniversary and commemorative moments. We look for those opportunities to celebrate with the fans, but also find this mutually beneficial partnership between both parties." This will be Cosm's sixth theatrical collaboration with Hollywood, having already partnered with Warner Bros. to bring "The Matrix," "Willy Wonka & the Chocolate Factory," "Harry Potter and the Sorcerer's Stone" and "It" to its locations. The company is set to launch immersive screenings of Universal's "Shrek" in December. Each Cosm dome has stadium-style seating, with booths and tables set on each level. The dome's width fills much of the viewers' periphery, giving the sensation that they are part of the onscreen environment. In this case, "Star Wars" will be displayed in a large rectangle in the center of the dome while the background is transformed into the iconic planets of Tatooine and Yavin IV that are featured in the film as well as the infamous Death Star. Audiences will also see elements that will make it appear like they're traveling at lightspeed and getting trapped in an intergalactic trash compactor. Cosm is working directly with studios Lucasfilm and Industrial Light and Magic as well as creative studio MakeMake to create the visuals and the sound mixing for the unique presentation of the film. "We look for those moments where sound, music ... listening to Darth Vader's breath for the first time ... you feel those moments differently in an 87-foot diameter dome and 12k resolution with the sound system we have," Scalise said. "And it's one of the things that with experiential cinema and our technology that we were so excited and honestly privileged that we can take these defining moments for fans and work closely with our partners that doesn't really change the authenticity of it, it just enhances it in a different manner." The premium experience will also be paired with a themed menu. Cosm has done this with other titles, such as "Harry Potter and the Sorcerer's Stone," serving guests throughout the screening with house-made shepherd's pie, pretzel wands with cheese dip and a box of Bertie Bott's Every Flavour Beans. Cosm is trying to establish itself as a destination for fandom — both for sports and for film. It has a wide variety of live event offerings, which it telecasts using proprietary cameras mounted in arenas that broadcast back to the dome, as well as its expanding library of movies. "What I love is that we really are kind of building these Cosm communities built on fandom," Scalise said. "It's the No. 1 foundation for our business." And Star Wars is a powerful fandom. The franchise remains one of the top-ranking pieces of intellectual property across film, television and retail annually, and Disney is gearing up for a massive celebration of its semicentennial including merchandise launches, theatrical re-releases, its biannual Star Wars Celebration convention and collaborations with other brands.

events.title: Alibaba-Megaspeed financing link traced via S’pore, Malaysia units, allegedly to buy Nvidia servers
events.summary: Speedmatrix, one of Megaspeed’s Malaysia subsidiaries, has an office in the Eco Botanic township in Johor. Alibaba-owned Singapore firm Apex had a financial arrangement with Megaspeed’s Malaysia unit, Speedmatrix, which pledged its computer equipment and other assets to Apex. Megaspeed, a major Nvidia chip buyer, is under US and Singapore scrutiny over possible chip diversion to China and suspected breaches of export laws. It has hired a US law firm to review compliance. Megaspeed’s overseas network spans five markets, with subsidiaries in Malaysia, Thailand, Indonesia, Australia and the US. SINGAPORE – A Singapore company owned by Chinese tech giant Alibaba had a financial arrangement with the Malaysian subsidiary of Megaspeed International, a major Nvidia chip buyer under scrutiny over the possible diversion of advanced artificial intelligence chips to China . Corporate records obtained by The Straits Times show that Speedmatrix, Megaspeed’s Malaysian subsidiary, pledged specified IT and network equipment, intellectual property and related rights to Apex Enterprise Solutions (Singapore) under an agreement dated June 18, 2024. The arrangement gave Apex security over the assets should Speedmatrix fail to meet certain contractual obligations. Malaysian corporate records show that the arrangement remained active as at Nov 11, 2026. The financial connection was highlighted in a May report by US short-seller Culper Research, which alleged that Alibaba may have channelled billions of dollars through Apex to finance Megaspeed’s purchases of Nvidia chips. The research firm, which had taken a position that would benefit from the fall of Nvidia’s share price, suggested that Alibaba had provided the funds to Apex, which may have passed a substantial portion to Megaspeed for distribution to its overseas subsidiaries. Apex was incorporated in Singapore in July 2023 and it is registered at Lazada One in Bras Basah Road, which is leased by Alibaba and its South-east Asian online shopping unit, Lazada Group. Accounting and Corporate Regulatory Authority records show that Apex’s immediate holding company is Cloud Intelligence (Cayman) Holding Limited. Its ultimate holding company is Alibaba Group Holding Limited, which is incorporated in the Cayman Islands and has contractual rights to Alibaba China’s profits. Apex, in its audited financial statement for the financial year ended March 31, 2025, described its business activity as “providing procurement activities”. Its corporate records also showed that Yuan Qian served as a director from August 2023 to August 2025. The name matches the Chinese name of Selina Yuan, a former Alibaba executive who has headed Alibaba Cloud’s international business in Singapore, but ST has not independently confirmed that she is the director named in Apex’s records. Apex’s current directors are Gong Zhengyuan, Zhu Bofu, and Madelyn Kwang Yeit Lam, a Singaporean who also serves as the company secretary. Kwang has also been listed as a director and secretary of Alibaba Cloud (Singapore) since 2016. She did not respond to ST’s queries. Apex’s auditor is PWC. When contacted, a spokesperson said: “This relates to a client matter, we are therefore unable to comment.” The Financial Times reported in November that Alibaba was one of Megaspeed’s major customers for its South-east Asian cloud service operation. Alibaba and Megaspeed did not respond to ST’s queries on the nature of their commercial relationships and whether the relationships have remained intact with investigations into Megaspeed. Megaspeed owns seven subsidiaries across five overseas markets, according to its financial statements for 2024, which are its latest publicly available records. Three are in Malaysia: Speedmatrix, Megaspeed International Sdn Bhd and MSFusion Sdn Bhd. All three are private limited companies. Speedmatrix and Megaspeed International Sdn Bhd were described as cloud-hosting service providers. MSFusion was classified as dormant at end-2024, but it entered a RM263.2 million (S$82.8 million) agreement to buy a site in Johor for a proposed data centre. Even so, MSFusion entered into a RM263.2 million (S$82.8 million) agreement to buy a site in Johor for a proposed data centre, according to the seller’s bourse filing in August 2025. Megaspeed also owned 99.99% of Megaspeed (Thailand) Co Ltd and 99% of PT Megaspeed International Indonesia, both cloud-hosting businesses. The other two Megaspeed’s wholly-owned subsidiaries are in Australia and the US. Megaspeed’s latest shipment recorded on corporate intelligence platform Sayari was to Speedmatrix – an Nvidia baseboard for high-performance graphics processing units, which arrived on Nov 18, 2025. The top receivers of Megaspeed’s shipments were Speedmatrix and PT Megaspeed International Indonesia, according to Sayari.

events.title: Canada’s ambassador warns Trump tariffs are driving up costs, threatening U.S. investment
events.summary: Canada’s ambassador to the U.S., Mark Wiseman, warned that uncertainty surrounding President Donald Trump’s tariffs is raising investment costs and discouraging businesses from expanding. New York Fed research found that roughly 90% of tariff costs were passed on to U.S. importers, with additional consumer price pressures expected in 2027. Canada is seeking to attract investment with a lower effective business tax rate, as trade tensions persist and Democrats prepare to challenge Trump’s tariffs in Congress. Canada's ambassador to the U.S. warned Wednesday that President Donald Trump's tariffs are driving up investment costs and discouraging business expansion, as new Federal Reserve research points to more price hikes for American consumers next year. "Uncertainty increases your cost of capital," Ambassador Mark Wiseman said at the B20 summit , a gathering of global business leaders in Washington hosted by the U.S. Chamber of Commerce. "If you're going to build a new plant, add a new shift, spend money on R&D, the more certainty you have, the more likely you're going to do that," said Wiseman, a former BlackRock executive who became Canada's ambassador in February. His warning comes as Washington and Ottawa struggle to resolve a tariff quarrel affecting one of the U.S.'s largest trading relationships. The two countries exchanged roughly $570 billion in goods during the first nine months of 2026, according to U.S. Census Bureau data . That's an increase from the same period in 2025, the first year of Trump's second term, but lower than the comparable nine months during the previous three years, when Joe Biden was president. U.S. customs duties calculated on imports from Canada reached $10 billion in 2025, compared with $400 million in 2024, according to the Congressional Research Service . An October study by New York Fed researchers found that nearly 90% of tariff costs were passed on to U.S. importers, with about a quarter of tariff increases eventually reaching consumer goods prices and further price pressures expected in 2027. The findings come as Labor Department data showed consumer prices rose a higher-than-expected 0.4% in October, adding to inflation concerns after Republicans' sweeping midterm losses . Trump has defended his tariffs as necessary to protect U.S. manufacturers and workers, accusing Canada of discriminatory trade practices that disadvantage U.S. exporters. The two governments have resumed negotiations after talks collapsed in August, with discussions focused on reducing tariffs on Canadian steel and automobiles. Trump has imposed duties of up to 50% on certain Canadian products , prompting retaliatory measures targeting billions of dollars in U.S. exports. Wiseman called for the removal of tariffs imposed under Sections 232 and 338 of U.S. trade law, saying a resolution would help businesses make long-term investment decisions. The political stakes have shifted following the midterms, with Democrats preparing to challenge Trump's tariffs when they take control of Congress in January. Still, Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney said Tuesday that the Trump administration remains Canada's principal negotiating partner. "We've had comprehensive free trade with the United States since 1988," Wiseman said, describing Canada's objective as returning "as close as we can to free trade" while creating the certainty businesses need. European ambassadors echoed those concerns at the B20 summit. Germany's ambassador to the U.S., Jens Hanefeld, said businesses could adapt to tariffs but struggled with an "ever-changing regulatory environment" that forced companies to spend more on lawyers to navigate shifting trade rules. Speaking on the same panel, France's ambassador, Aurélien Lechevallier, urged greater cooperation on AI and energy rather than continued trade disputes. "We've spent, I think, a lot of time the last years working and dealing with regulations, tariffs," he said. "Businesses are eager to do more business." — Correction: This story has been corrected to reflect that Wiseman spoke about adding shifts to plants. A previous version misquoted the ambassador.

events.title: Meet Colette Kress, the finance chief steering Nvidia through its first CEO transition
events.summary: Colette Kress, chief financial officer of Nvidia, has been named interim CEO. Nvidia Nvidia has named chief financial officer Colette Kress interim CEO after Jensen Huang resigned. Huang exited as Nvidia's board probed a foreign intelligence effort and his alleged affairs. Kress, seen as a potential successor, previously held finance roles at Cisco and Microsoft. Nvidia's longtime finance chief Colette Kress has been named interim CEO as a widening scandal brings Jensen Huang's 33-year tenure to an end. Kress's appointment on Thursday follows Huang's resignation , which the board said was effective immediately. The board said it is initiating a search for a permanent CEO and will "consider internal and external candidates." Nvidia's share price dropped 10% in premarket trading following the announcement. Huang stepped down after Nvidia's board opened an investigation into whether he was the target of a "foreign intelligence effort." He also admitted to being unfaithful to his wife in a memo. The New York Times reported that Huang had romantic relationships with Alice Huang, an executive at Nvidia customer Megaspeed — whom US intelligence officials identified as a suspected Chinese spy — as well as Kimberly Powell, an Nvidia employee who served as vice president of healthcare. Insiders and analysts had previously pointed to Kress as a likely successor to Huang, citing her visibility among shareholders. She has worked at Nvidia for 13 years, joining in September 2013 and helping to lead the company's finances through the AI boom. "NVIDIA's strength has always come from its people, and together with our leadership team, I am committed to building on the extraordinary foundation Jensen created over the last 33 years," Kress said in a statement on Thursday. Huang maintained a flat leadership structure with as many as 60 direct reports, and said he wanted to keep working for as long as possible, which complicated succession planning. Prior to joining Nvidia, Kress held finance positions at Cisco and Microsoft. She has also served at Texas Instruments in a variety of finance positions. Kress reported directly to Huang , Business Insider previously reported. Read the original article on Business Insider

events.title: Jensen Huang Resigns as Nvidia CEO
events.summary: Jensen Huang stepped down as the chief executive of Nvidia on Thursday, four days after the company announced its internal investigation into an affair he had with Alice Huang, also known as Huang Le, an alleged asset of China’s Ministry of State Security. “Jensen Huang has resigned as President, Chief Executive Officer, and a member of the Board, effective immediately,” the Nvidia board said in a statement. Nvidia’s chief financial officer, Colette Kress, will serve as interim CEO. The board said it “will consider internal and external candidates” for a permanent replacement. The board’s investigation was announced on November 8, slightly less than two weeks after The New York Times reported that the chief executive had been the target of a Chinese intelligence operation facilitated through his relationship with Alice Huang, who has no known relation to Jensen. The pair have been spotted in public together at least twice, in June 2024 and May 2025 . On November 11, The New York Times reported that Jensen Huang also allegedly had a relationship with a direct report at Nvidia. The alleged relationship with a subordinate, along with Huang’s business dealings with Megaspeed, a Singapore-based AI company where Alice Huang previously held a senior position, likely played a greater role in the board’s decision to oust Wang than the Chinese espionage allegations, a source familiar with the matter tells WIRED. US intelligence officials reportedly briefed President Donald Trump on Haung’s relationship with Alice last year, but the president did not act on it. On November 6, The New York Times and Financial Times reported that Alice was a spy for China's Ministry of State Security, and that she had been recruited to collect information on the Nvidia executive. (The Chinese government has rejected all claims that Alice was a spy for the country. ) Huang sent a companywide email on Sunday acknowledging his affair, apologizing to his family and Nvidia employees, and pledging cooperation with the internal investigation. The executive has been married to his wife Lori Huang since 1985 , and both of the couple’s two children work at the company. On Monday, WIRED exclusively reported that last year Huang began working with a crisis PR firm in order to manage his personal communications. In October 2025, those PR consultants started to be looped in to all press inquiries involving Huang, whether those inquiries were personal or professional in nature. The timing lines up with a New York Times report that month that the US Commerce Department was investigating whether Alice’s Megaspeed was helping Chinese companies get around American export controls with the help of a vast web of subsidiaries. The investigation was reportedly halted and transferred to the Justice Department after Nvidia general counsel Tim Teter inquired about it. Huang has been a vocal critic of these export controls, which he argues unnecessarily constrain the market for American chips, create discrete Chinese and American tech ecosystems, and spur China to build competitive chips of their own. Huang has worked to develop a relationship with Trump in order to advocate for policies that are advantageous for Nvidia, including the idea of opening its markets to China. Huang cofounded Nvidia in 1993 with friends Chris Malachowsky and Curtis Priem. The trio reportedly brainstormed their vision for the company in a Denny’s diner , and aspired to bring realistic 3D graphics to personal computers. For the first few decades of its existence, Nvidia was primarily known in the gaming community for creating chips powerful enough to render high-quality in-game graphics. In 2012, after a new kind of neural network known as AlexNet won a high-profile prize in computer vision, Nvidia pivoted from high-speed computer graphics to building chips that would support artificial intelligence. Huang has repeatedly said that the introduction of AlexNet, which was developed by AI engineers Alex Krizhevsky, Ilya Sutskever, and Geoffrey Hinton, was a “Big Bang”-like event for computing, Because its new GPUs proved highly effective at powering AI models that require massive amounts of processing power, the value of Nvidia shares soared in 2023 and 2024, in lockstep with the broader AI boom that began sweeping through the world economy. In the summer of 2025, Nvidia became the first company in history to cross $4 trillion in value. As of September 2026, the company controlled about 90 percent of the GPU market. Much of Nvidia’s epic rise over the few decades has been attributed not just to its cutting edge chips and its software “moat,” CUDA, that keeps developers locked into those chips; but also to the fast-thinking, controlling, charismatic, and often bombastic leadership style of Huang himself. Now, that critical part of the company’s success is on its way out the door.

events.title: Jensen Huang resigns as Nvidia CEO after affair with suspected Chinese spy
events.summary: Embattled Nvidia founder and chief executive Jensen Huang resigned on Thursday, marking a stunning fall from grace for the leader of a vital US computing giant that has long helped fuel the AI boom. Mr Huang’s departure came days after he admitted to having an affair with a woman suspected of being a Chinese spy. Nvidia's "board of directors announced today that Jensen Huang has resigned as president, chief executive officer, and a member of the Board, effective immediately," a statement from the chip giant read. Colette Kress, current executive vice president and chief financial officer, will serve as interim CEO, Nvidia added. Nvidia stock was down more than 10 per cent in pre-market trading. Harvey Jones, Chair of Nvidia's board of directors, said Ms Kress had helped lead Nvidia through a "period of extraordinary growth and has a deep understanding of our business, customers, operations and financial position". "She is supported by an experienced leadership team that has been instrumental in executing Nvidia's strategy and advancing its technology roadmap. Alice Huang affair Though not without controversy since he co-founded Nvidia in 1993, Mr Huang sparked a crisis in early November when he admitted to having an affair with a technology executive going by the name of Alice Huang. US officials and investigators said they believe Ms Huang to be a spy working on behalf of China, a top US rival in the tech and AI field. To maintain its AI edge, the US implemented various export policies designed to keep some of the most powerful US-made semiconductors and computers away from potentially adversarial countries. But Mr Huang and Nvidia were vocal in recent years in opposing such export policies, with the company’s chief executive saying the restrictions hurt US influence and prevented US technology from becoming a global standard. Proponents of the export policies, however, said the rules bolstered the US lead in a way that made it very difficult for countries like China to catch up, particularly in what’s considered the need for computing power to train AI language models. Some of those supporters of the export policies accused Nvidia and Mr Huang of simply wanting to boost revenue at all costs, even if it was to the detriment of US national security. As the overall mood toward AI, technology executives and unregulated technology began to sour among US voters, politicians increased scrutiny of Nvidia. By the time Mr Huang admitted to an affair with a technology executive, several media reports had accused his company of turning a blind eye to various products entering China. Mr Huang’s admission of infidelity expedited and amplified calls for investigations into his company. Shortly after Mr Huang’s mea culpa, Nvidia’s board of directors announced an independent investigation to address reports of whether he was the target of a foreign spy operation, and what, if anything had been compromised. Company representatives initially insisted Mr Huang would remain chief executive, but pressure grew. Mr Huang, along with Chris Malachowsky and Curtis Priem founded Nvidia in 1993 as the personal computer sector booming. A major part of that was gaming, but many computers at the time weren’t designed for the gamers, and that’s where Nvidia saw an opening. The company designed special graphics cards and video boards that while popular, didn’t necessarily make the Nvidia a household name. As a result, its name was mispronounced by many for a lengthy period of time. Profits steadily grew, however, and the company methodically expanded. As progress in AI started to hit its stride, Nvidia soon found its custom graphics processing units and boards in unprecedented demand. Nvidia could hardly build its products fast enough to keep up with demand, and yet it knew how to manufacture them to perfection. Revenue and profits skyrocketed, and Mr Huang’s presence became almost impossible to ignore, even among those who had zero interest in AI. His work ethic and mercurial management style became the stuff of legends. At one point, CBS did an interview inside a Denny’s restaurant where he spent many late nights founding the company. It was the sort of story that solidified what it meant to live the American dream, and yet as Nvidia and Mr Huang experienced unprecedented success, some US officials raised concerns that Nvidia’s profits were being generated at the expense of national security with the company’s products potentially being used by nefarious individuals and hostile governments. Mr Huang’s infidelity essentially was the straw that broke the camel’s back and left more questions about Nvidia’s governance. In the realm of US corporate drama, the departure of Mr Huang probably eclipses Apple’s dismissal of Steve Jobs back in 1985, which was mainly a boardroom power struggle.

events.title: AI titan Jensen Huang out as Nvidia CEO
events.summary: Can Trump find a way to work with Democrats? Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang steps down amid spy scandal and market loss Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has stepped down from the company following his reported affairs with a suspected Chinese spy as well as a Nvidia executive. The $4.2 trillion tech giant has lost more than $600bn in market value this week as Huang’s scandals rocked the company, which supplies most of the chips powering advanced AI technology. The stock slid more than 10 percent in pre-market trading on Thursday. The company appointed Colette Kress, Nvidia’s chief financial officer and executive vice president, as interim CEO on Thursday. Nvidia’s board met on Wednesday night to discuss ousting Huang, whose relationship with the alleged Chinese spy triggered investigations by the FBI, the United States Congress and the California-based tech giant. Nvidia is also facing a shareholder class-action lawsuit. The alleged Chinese intelligence asset, Alice Huang, is a former executive at Singapore-based Megaspeed, Nvidia’s primary business partner in southeast Asia. Founded in 2023, Megaspeed has been investigated over whether it helped Chinese companies access its $4.8bn stock of powerful Nvidia chips. The affair has raised national security concerns in the US, which restricts chip sales to China over concerns the Chinese military, intelligence agencies or companies could use the advanced technology. Huang, 63, is Nvidia’s co-founder, president and CEO. A close ally of United States President Donald Trump, he has pushed to ease US restrictions on chip exports to China. Trump said earlier this week that Huang told him he had “absolutely no idea” that he was in a relationship with an intelligence operative. Huang owns about 3.6 percent of Nvidia’s stock, making him one of the richest people in the world. He is a powerful figure in the AI industry, which has driven record stock market and wider economic gains. Nvidia’s board, which hired a law firm to investigate the affair with Alice Huang, met to decide Huang’s fate on Wednesday shortly after the New York Times reported that Huang also had an extramarital relationship with a Nvidia vice president who reports to him. Nvidia’s stock has tumbled since the scandal erupted, falling to a 14-year low, the Reuters news agency reported.

events.title: Trump says ‘we don’t need a deal with Iran’
events.summary: The U.S. should no longer seek a deal with Iran, President Donald Trump wrote on Truth Social. Trump directed Vice President JD Vance to instead focus his attention on corruption and crime in Democratic cities and states. "We don't need a deal with Iran. Those days have long since passed," Trump wrote in the post. The U.S. should no longer seek a deal with Iran, President Donald Trump said Thursday as he directed Vice President JD Vance to instead focus his attention on corruption and crime in Democratic cities and states. "We don't need a deal with Iran. Those days have long since passed," Trump wrote in a Truth Social post. "We've got their money, Hundreds of Billions of Dollars, and we've got their Strait!" Trump wrote, referring to the Strait of Hormuz, a key chokepoint in the ongoing U.S.-Iran war. The announcement came just over a week Republicans suffered huge losses in the midterm election. Vance and other Republicans have pinned those losses on the Iran war, which the U.S. and Israel started in late February. In the weeks leading up to Election Day, Trump repeatedly suggested the U.S. could resume launching military strikes, which have largely subsided as a testy stalemate has taken hold in the region The Wall Street Journal on Wednesday reported that Vance, who has led diplomatic efforts with Iran in prior months, was considering face-to-face talks with a top Iranian security official. Stock futures declined following Trump's post. The unpopular Iran war, which Trump and others in his administration would be won in a matter of weeks, is now in its ninth month with no clear end in sight. The conflict region has caused global energy prices to rise, creating a ripple effect through the economy and exacerbating concerns about inflation and affordability that were paramount to voters in the midterms. Corruption emerged as another top issue that broke in Democrats' favor in the election. Trump's post Thursday morning attempts to flip the script, blaming Democratic-run areas for allowing corruption and crime to proliferate. "I have asked Vice President Vance to focus his complete and total attention on the Massive Corruption and Crime taking place in Democrat run Cities and States throughout the U.S.," Trump wrote. "The Blue States, such as Minnesota, California, Illinois, and many more, are all poorly run, corrupt disasters. Billions of Dollars is being stolen each and every month," the president wrote. "Our Budget could be quickly BALANCED with the correction of this large scale criminal activity." "CORRUPTION is in the Democrat Leadership's blood!" he added. This is breaking news. events.title: NVIDIA Announces CEO Transition
events.summary: Colette Kress, Executive Vice President and Chief Financial Officer, Appointed Interim CEO Harvey C. Jones Appointed First-Ever Chair of the Board NVIDIA (NASDAQ: NVDA) Board of Directors announced today that Jensen Huang has resigned as President, Chief Executive Officer, and a member of the Board, effective immediately. Colette Kress, current Executive Vice President and Chief Financial Officer of NVIDIA, has agreed to serve as Interim Chief Executive Officer. Kress will continue to serve as Executive Vice President and Chief Financial Officer while serving as Interim Chief Executive Officer until a permanent successor has been named. The Board is initiating a search for a permanent Chief Executive Officer and will consider internal and external candidates. Kress has served as Executive Vice President and Chief Financial Officer of NVIDIA since joining the company in September 2013. During her tenure, she has led the company’s finance organization and has played a key role in NVIDIA’s growth and evolution. Prior to joining NVIDIA, Kress spent nearly 25 years in finance roles at leading technology companies, including Cisco and Microsoft. The Board of Directors appointed Harvey C. Jones as its first-ever Chair of the Board. Mr. Jones has been an entrepreneur, technology executive, and active venture investor for over 30 years, including serving as Chief Executive Officer and Executive Chairman of Synopsys. “Colette has helped lead NVIDIA through a period of extraordinary growth and has a deep understanding of our business, customers, operations and financial position,” said Harvey Jones, Chair of the NVIDIA Board of Directors. “She is supported by an experienced leadership team that has been instrumental in executing NVIDIA’s strategy and advancing its technology roadmap. The Board has full confidence in Colette and the leadership team, and we expect the company’s operations, customer commitments and product roadmap to continue without interruption.” “NVIDIA’s strength has always come from its people, and together with our leadership team, I am committed to building on the extraordinary foundation Jensen created over the last 33 years,” said Colette Kress, Interim CEO and CFO, NVIDIA. “We will continue advancing the work that has made NVIDIA a leader in accelerated computing and AI, and execute on the opportunities ahead. Our focus remains on serving our customers, partners, developers and shareholders.” Jensen’s contributions to NVIDIA are profound. NVIDIA is one of the most consequential technology companies in the world. The Board and the company thank Jensen for his immeasurable contributions to the company and the industry. NVIDIA will report its third-quarter fiscal 2027 financial results on Tuesday, November 17, at approximately 1:20 p.m. PT, as previously scheduled, followed by its earnings call at 2 p.m. PT. events.title: Poundland owner secures two extra weeks to ensure retail chain’s survival
events.summary: US investment firm Gordon Brothers is ‘taking due care’ to consider if one of three bidders has enough funds Poundland’s owner has said it is “taking due care” to consider if one of three bidders had enough funds to ensure its survival after the troubled budget retail chain secured two more weeks to find a deal. The management of Poundland , which employs approximately 12,000 people and operates 600 stores in the UK and Ireland, won approval from the high court for an extension of legal protection from creditors on Thursday morning. Poundland’s board said it had sought the extra time “with a view to identifying the best available prospects for shareholders, creditors and our people”. It added: “Our stores remain open as usual during this period and we thank our colleagues, suppliers and customers for their incredible and continued support.” The retail chain’s owner, the US investment firm Gordon Brothers, has been under pressure to accept a bid for the company that would save retail jobs and protect thousands of suppliers since Poundland filed a notice of intention to appoint administrators two weeks ago. A spokesperson for Gordon Brothers said on Thursday: “We support the board’s decision to extend the legal moratorium over the company by a further 10 working days. This brings additional stability amid an ongoing sale process in the backdrop of increasing cost pressures and a difficult inflationary economic environment. “With this decision, we are today able to confirm to Poundland employees that funds will be released to allow payroll to be made in full this month, while additional funds continue to be released to support Poundland’s ongoing trading. “We are in discussions with three parties for a sale of the whole business, and we have also received several offers from established high street retailers for significant parts of the business. “While our preference remains a sale of the whole company, we are taking due care to ensure that any successful offer can provide the funds required to acquire the business and see it through to sustainable cash generation. We, the board, and all involved are working to secure a credible plan that delivers certainty, preserves value and protects as many jobs as possible.” Gordon Brothers confirmed it had provided £85m of financing, understood to be via an asset-backed loan that Poundland has only partially used over the past year. That financing is in addition to a £30m shareholder loan largely taken on by Gordon Brothers when it bought the business for a nominal £1 last year. Gordon Brothers fought back after MPs on Wednesday accused the Poundland owner of extracting millions of pounds from the retailer when it was on a “knife-edge”. Documents provided to MPs showed the finance firm had taken close to £20m in interest payments and various fees, including those relating to store closures since acquiring Poundland. Gordon Brothers said it had provided finance for Poundland “when no one else was willing to finance the company – and has contributed substantial efforts to support a turnaround. “Had we not, the company would have collapsed into insolvency in August 2025. Our efforts have continuously focused on the company’s value and its people, not prioritising one over the other.”

events.title: Deloitte is cutting GLP-1 coverage for weight loss and raising health insurance costs for US staff
events.summary: Healthcare costs are rising, and Deloitte told staff it was "untenable" to swallow those costs alone. Peter Dazeley/Getty Images Deloitte is joining a growing number of US companies cutting GLP-1s for weight loss from benefits. It is also raising staff health insurance costs, according to a document seen by Business Insider. Deloitte US told employees it was "untenable" to swallow the rising cost of healthcare alone. Deloitte's US employees are joining the growing list of workers facing more expensive and less generous healthcare benefits. The Big Four firm will no longer cover GLP-1 medication for weight-loss purposes through its medical plans, according to an internal benefits guide seen by Business Insider. At the same time, Deloitte employees will also face higher deductibles and out-of-pocket maximums under most health plans, the document said, meaning higher costs both before and after coverage kicks in. The changes come as corporate America battles a widespread rise in health insurance costs for both employees and employers. Deloitte told staff in the document that the changes "reflect the hard trade-offs of today's cost environment," and that there was a need "for shared responsibility in a few specific places where it's become untenable for Deloitte to carry the cost alone." GLP-1 medication will remain covered when prescribed for diabetes and other covered medical conditions, the document said. For those seeking support with weight loss, Deloitte is instead offering employees access to a virtual lifestyle program called eMed that includes coaching and a $125-per-prescription employer contribution. List prices for common GLP-1s like semaglutide and tirzepatide are generally in excess of $1,000, though direct purchase programs such as LillyDirect and government plans like TrumpRx mean the costs are often significantly lower. TrumpRx, for instance, offers semaglutide injection pens under the Ozempic brand name for between $199 and $499. A Deloitte spokesperson told Business Insider that, like other large employers, the firm has made select modifications where cost growth rates are no longer sustainable. The new support for weight-related uses of GLP-1s includes direct-from-manufacturer drug pricing, they said. "Our financial commitment to our people and their families continues to grow," the spokesperson said. Have a tip to share? Contact this reporter via email at pthompson@businessinsider.com or Signal at Polly_Thompson.89. Use a personal email address, a nonwork WiFi network, and a nonwork device; here's our guide to sharing information securely . Deloitte is also expanding certain healthcare coverage, including improving long-term disability protection and adding free annual eye exams to its company-paid discount vision program. The benefits guide seen by Business Insider applies to what Deloitte calls its "Core, Domain, and Enterprise professionals," which includes the majority of its traditional client-facing accountants, consultants, and technical specialists. The firm employs about 181,000 people in the US. Health insurance costs are rising across the board Deloitte is one of many employers cutting GLP-1 coverage for weight loss purposes. Michael Siluk/UCG/Universal Images Group via Getty Images Deloitte's changes to its coverage mirror a broader squeeze on US employer health plans. As healthcare costs and demand climb, everyone is paying more. A 2026 health benefits survey from KFF found that workers on a family plan paid an average of $7,471 a year in premiums — a 9% increase from 2025. When accounting for employer contributions, family plan premiums totaled $28,303 in 2026, a roughly 5% increase from 2025. Restricting eligibility for GLP-1s has become a common route for employers looking to curb healthcare spending. The drugs were developed to treat diabetes, but have become sought-after treatments for obesity and related chronic conditions. Aon, an insurance broker and employee-benefits consultancy, found that use of GLP-1s was up 75% in 2025. The drugs' rapid uptake and potential for long-term use have made them a costly pressure point for insurers and employer health plans. Aon found that 39% of employers planned to reduce or restrict GLP-1 coverage in 2026. PwC and Starbucks are among those that have pulled back their coverage for weight-loss purposes this year. Deloitte has also introduced broader benefit changes for a select group of staff. In April, Business Insider reported that for staff in Deloitte's Center talent model — which mostly includes internal-facing admin roles — parental leave, annual PTO, and IVF funding would be reduced or eliminated as of January 1, 2027. Deloitte's Americas division was its slowest-growing region globally in the financial year ending May 31, 2026, with revenue rising 3.2%, down from 7.1% growth a year earlier. AWS New Horizon Digicert Netscout Resources Intelligence Webinars & Events Newsletters New unit sports more qubits and is planned to be part of future fault-tolerant rig AMD: Where we're going we don't need (as much) DRAM 1 day ago AMD's Epyc X-chips are back after a three-year hiatus 1 day ago A closer look at Verano, AMD's first step toward a Zen-based superchip to rival Nvidia's Vera Rubin 1 day ago EU's €212M border IT project lands IBM and Atos in legal water 2 days ago Anthropic's super bug-finding Mythos model is going into Cisco and IBM products 2 days ago IBM has unveiled the Nighthawk r3, an upcoming next-gen quantum processor that will feature 520 qubits, as another step towards a planned fault-tolerant quantum system it hopes to launch in 2029. Big Blue's current Nighthawk r2 was only made available in September and features 120 quantum bits (qubits) capable of handling circuits using 7,500 operations. Its successor, IBM claims, will have more than four times as many qubits and execute 10,000 quantum operations to tackle larger, more complex problems while maintaining the same speed and accuracy. Nighthawk r3 is slated to arrive in 2027, when Big Blue plans to link two of the quantum processors into a single system with more than 1,000 qubits. IBM said applications increasingly require circuits executing thousands of quantum operations on approximately 100 qubits or more, speeding up collection of the millions or billions of samples needed to perform complex computations. Speed determines whether such demanding workloads can be completed in practical timeframes and at a reasonable cost. The new quantum processor will feature 10 chip-to-chip interconnects, called l-couplers, designed for linking together processors that it will use to enable a single 1,040-qubit system. This tech was tested using Nighthawk r1 processors . IBM previously outlined its goal of reaching reliable error correcting territory in 2029 with a quantum processor codenamed Starling. Now it intends for this to be the world’s first fault-tolerant quantum computer , capable of running quantum circuits comprising 100 million quantum operations on 200 logical qubits. This is an ambitious goal, considering fault-tolerant quantum technology always seems to be at least a decade away, despite numerous breakthroughs and technology introductions. However, some in the technology industry believe the odds on a working system are shortening , given the increased activity around making encryption ready with support for quantum-resistant algorithms. Then again, a professor at the University of Auckland New Zealand famously claimed last year that quantum computers hadn't so far managed to factor any number greater than 21 without cheating. IBM presented a framework for Starling in a 2025 paper outlining hardware to implement the improbably named bivariate bicycle quantum low-density parity check (qLDPC) error correction codes. These significantly reduce the number of physical qubits needed to store and process quantum information, compared to existing surface codes. Using the architecture in the paper, Big Blue intends to assemble Starling from modules that each contain a quantum memory and logical processing unit (LPU), allowing logic operations on the memory. The modules will have universal adapters letting them connect using l-couplers. IBM is also preparing the way ahead by combining its quantum processors with classical high-performance compute (HPC) systems to research better quantum error correction. Last week, Oak Ridge National Laboratory (ORNL) in the US announced such a system , combining an IBM Quantum System Two with Nighthawk r2 quantum processors and Umbra, powered by AMD 5th Gen Epyc CPUs and Instinct MI355X GPU accelerators. IBM also has a partnership with Japan's RIKEN scientific research institute under which an IBM Quantum System Two has been integrated with the Fugaku Arm-based supercomputer, once the most powerful system in the world.

events.title: Faisal Islam: Why the UK economy is surprisingly resilient
events.summary: Published 12 November 2026, 13:26 GMT The UK economy grew at its fastest rate for more than two years in the three months to September. "Top gear" and "strikingly strong" were among the descriptions of the 0.7% growth offered by the economists who track every minor murmur of Britain's economy. It is an upgrade on "solid" and "resilient", and in turn a world away from "hardest hit by the Iran War". Against the backdrop of the world's biggest disruption to energy flows, rising market borrowing costs - and the cruel summers since the pandemic - it is impressive growth. It should reset some of the swirl of self-reinforcing negativity. The UK's economic growth has averaged less than 0.1% in the four Q3s [ie July to September] since the pandemic. The average prediction just months ago for this July to September was just 0.1%. Even the UK's official forecaster the Office for Budget Responsibility (OBR) effectively pencilled in 0.3% at the Budget just 3 weeks ago. This figure has not been exceeded outside the pandemic since 2017. It puts the UK on course to be the second fastest growing economy after the US across the major G7 countries which also includes Canada, Japan, Germany, Italy and France. It is tempting to think about what the economy would have done if the Iran War hadn't happened. If interest rates had been cut instead of their recent rise. While the latest figure kills the doom, it is clearly not a boom either. Spending on AI and tech have driven the surprise upside over the year. While the AI data centre boom may at any point turn to bust, these figures suggest that spending across the economy on investing in these technologies is helpingboost growth. Consumers have been resilient, at least till the autumn, perhaps helped by better economic vibes. While there has been an understandable focus on high UK borrowing costs, another measure of the international standing of the UK economy, sterling's value, reached post Brexit referendum highs last week. Productivity and investment is also looking stronger, especially after recent revisions. Some of the most encouraging figures are in private sector business investment. I spoke to the chancellor at Nexeon in Oxfordshire, which is searching for a UK factory to manufacture its cutting edge electric vehicle battery - and British - technology. My colleagues visited British watchmakers in Maidenhead carving out a niche to take on the Swiss. However, this may well not last for the final three months of the year. Consumer confidence has already fallen as petrol and domestic energy prices start to rise again. There is a significant challenge with everyday cost-of-living pressures in the coming months. Construction and private house building remain depressed. The Iran conflict remains the big unknown and whether post the US midterm elections there could be a durable end to the conflict in the Gulf. Some oil and gas production there is starting to normalise. It could bring down petrol prices, energy bills, government borrowing costs, and mortgage costs too. Expect to see Downing Street investing heavily in "settlement of the conflict", which the chancellor told me is the "best economic policy". events.title: Washington risks misinterpreting Iran's 'peacemaker', according to analyst
events.summary: Washington is at risk of mistaking Mohsen Rezaei’s new prominence for a willingness to make concessions, Iran analyst Alex Vatanka argues. The former Revolutionary Guards commander, now secretary of Iran’s Supreme National Security Council, has received a letter from US Vice President JD Vance and is reportedly seen by American intelligence as the figure best placed to deliver a deal across Tehran’s factious institutions. But Rezaei’s comeback owes little to public legitimacy — he lost four presidential bids and his economic ideas were widely mocked — and much to a leadership vacuum left by the war and a network of IRGC loyalists built over decades, Vatanka writes for the Saudi-owned magazine Al Majalla. Rezaei has already shown the limits of his flexibility. He welcomed the letter’s tone, then insisted Washington accept Iran’s conditions first. Yesterday he went further, telling Al Mayadeen that not “ a single speck ” of enriched uranium would leave the country because Iran needs it to build nuclear-powered submarines — a rejection of the core US demand. His appointment was itself a product of hardline frustration: Rezaei was elevated by people close to Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei who were unhappy with parliament speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf’s handling of the talks, a Crisis Group analyst told Radio Free Europe . — Ed Clowes
